instruction: Purge Orphan Datablocks `init_file/scene.blend` contains one mesh object `Cube` whose sole material `Mat_InUse` (in slot 0) references an image `Img_InUse` via an Image Texture node. The file is cluttered with 20 unused materials (named `Mat_Orphan_00`.. `Mat_Orphan_19`) and 5 unused images (named `Img_Orphan_0`.. `Img_Orphan_4`). These orphans are not assigned to any object, material, texture, or node — they are kept alive only by a fake-user flag. Remove every orphan material and image from the file without disturbing `Cube` or any datablock that is actually in use, and save the result to `output/answer.blend` (relative to the working directory). 1. `output/answer.blend` exists and opens as a valid Blender file. 2. A mesh object named `Cube` still exists in the scene. 3. `Cube`'s first material slot still holds a material named `Mat_InUse`. 4. A material named `Mat_InUse` exists in `bpy.data.materials`. 5. An image named `Img_InUse` exists in `bpy.data.images`. 6. No material whose name starts with `Mat_Orphan_` exists in `bpy.data.materials`. 7. No image whose name starts with `Img_Orphan_` exists in `bpy.data.images`. 8. `len(bpy.data.materials)` equals exactly 1. 9. The number of user-created images in `bpy.data.images` — excluding Blender's auto-created `Render Result` and `Viewer Node` entries — equals exactly 1. Do not delete or rename `Cube`, its mesh, its material slot, or any in-use datablock.
source: Blender Manual — Outliner Orphan Data and Purge
